basis.evidenceSnippet: Guidelines for Generative AI in Education: The Education Board has approved guidelines for the use of generative AI in first and second-cycle education. This document establishes a framework to ensure transparency, fairness and security in the integration of AI into teaching, learning and assessment. [Guidelines for the use of Generative AI in First and Second-Cycle Education at Lund University (pdf)]
Stöd i lärande och forskning. Användning av generativ AI ska stödja lärande och forskning och ersätter inte grundläggande färdigheter, kritiskt tänkande eller vetenskaplig metod.

Medarbetare och studenter är ansvariga för allt innehåll de producerar, oavsett om generativ AI har använts som stöd. Det är den enskildes ansvar att säkerställa att materialet uppfyller krav på korrekthet och akademisk integritet.

If you wish to use GenAI for a compulsory assignment or in an examination, you must always double-check with the teacher whether it is permitted and, if so, how you should report its use. Even if it is not clearly stated in the course materials that GenAI is prohibited, it may still be considered cheating if you make it appear as though you have created something yourself that a GenAI tool has generated for you.

You may not write or upload sensitive material or sensitive personal data according to GDPR, such as: health information; ethnic origin; political opinions; religious beliefs; trade union membership; sex life or sexual orientation; biometric or genetic data. You may also never upload medical information regardless of confidentiality status.

At Lund University, it is permissible to use generative AI tools in education if you believe they can contribute to or facilitate learning. However, there are some important things to consider. As a teacher, you need to: be able to confirm that students have achieved the program's and course's learning objectives; be aware that sharing students' work with GAI tools is not allowed; ensure that every student has equal access to the GAI tools you recommend; inform students about the risks of sharing personal information or copyrighted material with the tools; inform students about the rules for using GAI tools in the course or program.

Once you have reviewed learning objectives and made decisions about the use of GenAI products in teaching, you must inform your students. Be clear about whether and, if so, how students can use GenAI products in their work. It is also important to inform students about the consequences of unauthorized use of GenAI products:

When studying, you should primarily use the tools for which Lund University holds licences. As a student at Lund University, you can use Microsoft Copilot Chat and Google Gemini by logging in with your student account. However, even if you are logged in with your student account, you must never upload, for example, other students' work, sensitive personal data or copyright-protected material - this applies to text as well as images, audio or video.

claim-lund-student-exam-permission.text: Lund University's student guidance says students who want to use GenAI for a compulsory assignment or examination must check whether it is permitted and how to report its use; presenting GenAI-generated work as one's own may be treated as cheating.
claim-lund-student-exam-permission.scope: For a compulsory assignment, check with the teacher whether GenAI is permitted and how to report it; silence in course materials is not permission.

evidence.quote: If you wish to use GenAI for a compulsory assignment or in an examination, you must always double-check with the teacher whether it is permitted and, if so, how you should report its use. Even if it is not clearly stated in the course materials that GenAI is prohibited, it may still be considered cheating if you make it appear as though you have created something yourself that a GenAI tool has generated for you.
evidence.location: Be open with your teachers

claim-lund-student-licensed-tools-privac.text: Lund University's student guidance says students should primarily use Lund-licensed tools such as Microsoft Copilot Chat and Google Gemini, and must not upload other students' work, sensitive personal data, or copyright-protected material.
claim-lund-student-licensed-tools-privac.scope: Student guidance prohibits uploading other students’ work, sensitive personal data or protected material, even with a student login; staff ChatGPT guidance also excludes medical information.

evidence.quote: When studying, you should primarily use the tools for which Lund University holds licences. As a student at Lund University, you can use Microsoft Copilot Chat and Google Gemini by logging in with your student account. However, even if you are logged in with your student account, you must never upload, for example, other students' work, sensitive personal data or copyright-protected material - this applies to text as well as images, audio or video.
evidence.location: Protect your privacy and that of others

claim-lund-chatgpt-sensitive-data.text: Lund University's staff AI page says users may not write or upload sensitive material or sensitive personal data to ChatGPT, and may never upload medical information regardless of confidentiality status.
claim-lund-chatgpt-sensitive-data.scope: Student guidance prohibits uploading other students’ work, sensitive personal data or protected material, even with a student login; staff ChatGPT guidance also excludes medical information.

evidence.quote: You may not write or upload sensitive material or sensitive personal data according to GDPR, such as: health information; ethnic origin; political opinions; religious beliefs; trade union membership; sex life or sexual orientation; biometric or genetic data. You may also never upload medical information regardless of confidentiality status.
evidence.location: ChatGPT - What is prohibited to write or upload?

claim-lund-policy-learning-support.text: Lund University's Swedish policy says generative AI use is to support learning and research and does not replace basic skills, critical thinking, or scientific method.
claim-lund-policy-learning-support.scope: The policy describes GenAI as support for learning and research, not a replacement for basic skills, critical thinking or scientific method.

evidence.quote: Stöd i lärande och forskning. Användning av generativ AI ska stödja lärande och forskning och ersätter inte grundläggande färdigheter, kritiskt tänkande eller vetenskaplig metod.
evidence.location: Principer - Stöd i lärande och forskning

claim-lund-policy-content-responsibility.text: Lund University's Swedish policy says staff and students are responsible for all content they produce, including when generative AI has been used as support.
claim-lund-policy-content-responsibility.scope: Staff and students remain responsible for their content. Passing off generated work as your own may be treated as cheating.

evidence.quote: Medarbetare och studenter är ansvariga för allt innehåll de producerar, oavsett om generativ AI har använts som stöd. Det är den enskildes ansvar att säkerställa att materialet uppfyller krav på korrekthet och akademisk integritet.
evidence.location: Principer - Ansvarig för innehåll

claim-lund-education-permissible-teacher.text: Lund University's GenAI Q&A says generative AI tools are permissible in education when teachers believe they contribute to or facilitate learning, with teachers responsible for informing students about course or programme rules.
claim-lund-education-permissible-teacher.scope: Teacher guidance calls for clear course rules, learning-outcome checks and equal access; it also says students’ work must not be shared with GenAI tools.

evidence.quote: At Lund University, it is permissible to use generative AI tools in education if you believe they can contribute to or facilitate learning. However, there are some important things to consider. As a teacher, you need to: be able to confirm that students have achieved the program's and course's learning objectives; be aware that sharing students' work with GAI tools is not allowed; ensure that every student has equal access to the GAI tools you recommend; inform students about the risks of sharing personal information or copyrighted material with the tools; inform students about the rules for using GAI tools in the course or program.
evidence.location: Questions about rules and guidelines - What are the guidelines at Lund University?

claim-lund-teachers-inform-students.text: Lund University's teacher guidance says teachers should inform students after deciding how GenAI products may be used in teaching and should explain whether and how students can use GenAI products in their work.
claim-lund-teachers-inform-students.scope: Teacher guidance calls for clear course rules, learning-outcome checks and equal access; it also says students’ work must not be shared with GenAI tools.

evidence.quote: Once you have reviewed learning objectives and made decisions about the use of GenAI products in teaching, you must inform your students. Be clear about whether and, if so, how students can use GenAI products in their work. It is also important to inform students about the consequences of unauthorized use of GenAI products:
evidence.location: Step 4: Inform your students
